The seven-string guitar is often credited to Andrei Sychra, but the guitar historian Matanya Ophee points out that seven-string classical guitars may already have existed in Europe at the time. Sychra wrote more than a thousand works for seven strings, some reprinted in the 1840s and the 1880s and published again in the Soviet Union in 1926. At the end of the nineteenth century and the beginning of the twentieth there were also a nine-string method book and ten-string romantic guitars. In the twentieth century the Swedish luthier Georg Bolin developed the eleven-string alto guitar in the 1960s; Paul Galbraith and David Rubio also developed the eight-string Brahms guitar.
